script: He diagnosed Stalin with paranoia, and was dead the next day. In December 1927, the Soviet Union's most respected neurologist was summoned to the Kremlin to examine Stalin privately, no witnesses, no official record of what was said. He walked out of that meeting and went straight back to a medical conference, where he told colleagues exactly what he had found inside that room: a paranoiac with a withered arm. He said it in passing, almost casually, as if it were just another diagnosis. By the next morning, he was dead. Officials moved fast: only his brain was examined, and his body was cremated that same day, leaving nothing behind to investigate later. Soviet authorities quietly erased his name from every medical textbook, and it stayed erased for decades, until Stalin himself finally died. Officials called it natural causes. Nobody who actually knew him ever believed that for a second. He diagnosed Stalin with paranoia, and paid for those few words with his life within a single day.

title: The Soviet Doctor Who Diagnosed Stalin, and Died Within a Day
description:
In 1927, the USSR's top neurologist examined Stalin and called him a paranoiac in front of colleagues. He was dead within a day, and his name was erased from Soviet medicine until Stalin himself died decades later.
